newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian share market retreats in lower turnover.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian share market retreats in lower turnover.

text.p: Hungarian share prices fell for the second successive day on Thursday and traders saw hardly any signs of a substantial recovery in view of a lack of corporate news and fears of a U.S. rate hike.

"Investors are very cautious with the international market sentiment being the same," a trader said, adding that investors were wary also on the central European region. "A rate hike in the U.S. may have a knock-on effect on the emerging markets."
The BUX index closed at 5,069.30 points, down 68.24.
BUX futures weakened for all maturities by between 85.00 and 115.00 points. June BUX futures fell 93 points to 5,267.5.

While foreign markets move mostly downwards spreading their negative effect to the Hungarian bourse, the market receives hardly any support from the domestic corporate side, the trader said, expecting the market to head down on Friday.
However, on Thursday, retail group Csopak was said benefiting from its plan to pay a 10 percent dividend on the 1996 results against an eight percent dividend on 1995.
Csopak, well outperforming the day's almost all gainers, closed nearly four percent higher at 3,090 forints.
"The rise is clearly the result of the higher dividend ratio," one trader said. "This is so, despite the fact that the dividend ratio is below the inflation."
Elsewhere on the market, tile maker Zalakeramia, whose shareholders approved a capital increase on Wednesday to finance acqusitions, remained untraded on Thursday.
"Zalakeramia's market is completely dead," one trader said. "There would be sellers but like on the whole market, it is very difficult to sell bigger share packages."
Thursday's leading losers included OTP Bank which fell nearly four percent or 135 forints to end at 3,305 and the two chemicals.
TVK lost three percent or 65 forints to end at 2,040, while Borsodchem eased two and a half percent to close at 5,990 forints.
